thread.title: Union turn 2-goal lead into Toronto draw after historic Gavran goalie goal
thread.title_full: Union turn 2-goal lead into Toronto draw after historic Gavran goalie goal

author: Matthew DeGeorge
title: Union turn 2-goal lead into Toronto draw after historic Gavran goalie goal
text:
Trinity Audioplayer ready...
The Philadelphia Union have, for most of the 2026 season, been merely bad.
Wednesday night, they added farcical to the repertoire.
The Union blew a two-goal lead in Toronto, then took the lead in the 89th minute – then allowed just the third goalkeeper goal in MLS history to Luka Gavran in the sixth minute of stoppage time to slump to an ignominious 3-3 draw at BMO Field.
In a season where the Union (1-6-2, 5 points) have been run-of-the-mill underwhelming in a field full of contenders for the title of lousiest team in the East, they may have unlocked something new north of the border, on a night after which only Atlanta United’s fecklessness keeps them out of the standings basement.
Saturday at home, the Union couldn’t create anything offensively but also relented nothing in a 0-0 draw with D.C. United (which itself Wednesday went from four games without a goal to four goals at New York Red Bulls in a 4-4 draw. Again, the East may be dreadful.)
Wednesday, the Union scored first for the first time all season on the kind of counterattacking goal that won them the Supporters’ Shield last year, with Milan Iloski running in behind in the fifth minute of first-half stoppage time and Jovan Lukic finding him with a measured through ball.
They took their first multi-goal lead of the season in the 52nd when Danley Jean Jacques scored … or rather, Jean Jacques’ pressure meant that an attempted clearance from Toronto center back Zane Monlouis caromed off Jean Jacques’ shin and past Gavran.
“We scored our first goal in a really nice transitional moment and had them on the ropes a little bit,” coach Bradley Carnell said. “But you can’t be coming away from home, taking the lead three times and giving up the lead. So felt that this was two points lost today for sure. And we continue fighting.”
That should’ve a harbinger of the chaos to come. Four straight halves without conceding a goal ended in the 56th minute when Josh Sargent bamboozled the Union defense, stupefying Nathan Harriel and Olwethu Makhanya far too easily to give the Reds a foothold. Kobe Franklin scored eight minutes later to level the game in the 64th, Makhanya marooned in midfield while Franklin ran around him and pinged a ball off the far post and in.
“They started stressing us a little bit on the wider areas. (Jonathan) Osorio started rolling out and pushing Franklin up a little bit higher, and then (Malik) Henry comes in and makes a difference to the game in the 1-v-1s on the sidelines,” Carnell said. “So we were protecting the middle of the field. But there’s a couple of moments where we don’t really defend one-vs.-one in the way that we usually do, in a capacity that I know we can, which is just a little bit unfortunate.”
That seemed conquerable, when Harriel headed home Alejandro Bedoya’s flicked-on front-post header of a Jesus Bueno corner kick in the 89th.
But it wouldn’t be. Because in the sixth minute of stoppage time (beyond the minimum of five shown on the board), Gavran jumped into the mix on a free kick. He watched the delivery from the left flank sail through the box, then a follow from the right wing fizzle over traffic. Then everyone on the Union watched the 6-5 goalie drift to the penalty spot, leap between a clueless Ezekiel Alladoh and a slow-to-react Makhanya and snap a header past Andre Blake.
With the goal, Gavran became just the third goalkeeper in MLS history to score, joining Danny Cepero for the New York Red Bulls in 2008 and Will Hesmer for Columbus in 2012 (also in Toronto).
Gavran also moved ahead of Union striker Bruno Damiani in scoring this season (0 goals in 759 minutes), and he jumped past Alladoh in shots on target this season (again 0, in 326 minutes).
It’s a brutal way to lose a game, against a team that itself played some brutal soccer. But it’s also where the Union are at this moment, hovering over rock bottom in the East.
And it’s now incumbent on them to make sure it’s the outlier rather than the norm as the team visits Columbus on Saturday.
“I think the trend has been really good from us,” Carnell said. “I think we’ve been really strong defensively. And I would say this was an anomaly for what I’ve seen over the last couple of weeks. So, I don’t want to say that there’s any panic stations now. We just have to make this one hurt for a few minutes now. We have a long road trip, and the minute we touch down in Columbus, we have to let that go.”

Four straight halves without conceding a goal ended in the 56th minute when Josh Sargent bamboozled the Union defense, stupefying Nathan Harriel and Olwethu Makhanya far too easily to give the Reds a foothold.
